_notes: Locally added -- upstream pinmame-nvram-maps has no map for CSI.
Built from a 4-player game driven through the cabinet's own streamer.
current_player and current_ball are adjacent in CPU RAM at 0x0003443C and 0x0003443D, player low
and ball high, the shape every Stern SAM game measured uses.
Scores are 4 bytes on 8-byte centres from 0x021109F0. The sweep also offered 0x00033784 on 4-byte
centres in CPU RAM, reading 601,580 / 150,440 / 15,040 / 9,400 -- each roughly a quarter of the
one before, which is a scaled or derived set rather than a scoreboard. Scores live in NVRAM on
every SAM game measured, which is what settles it.
player_count at 0x02110900, the one address every SAM game shares.
Five high score records from 0x02102B98, bounded by where the 16-bit checksum stops validating.
This game has no mode champions: the block ends at five and the machine's post-game DMD cycle
shows no champion entries, unlike Avatar, Dark Knight and Big Buck Hunter.
Only csi_240 is claimed; SAM addresses move between revisions.
Confirmed after the table exited: the map decodes that game as 4 players scoring 945,250 /
Free Play was not toggled on this game. Its address is derived, and the derivation is worth
stating because it is testable rather than assumed. Machine adjustments are an array of 8-byte
records from 0x02102008 -- a 32-bit little-endian value, then a byte holding 0xFF minus the sum
of the value's four bytes, padded 0xFF above. Every record in every image checked satisfies it.
Aligning this game's array against a game where Free Play was measured puts it at one of only
two positions across all twenty SAM games examined, and the value there reads 1 on a cabinet
that is in free play. The alignment was validated prospectively: on nba_802 and smanve_101 --
the two games where alignment agreement was weakest -- the address was predicted first, then
confirmed by toggling, and both were exact.
Writing this field requires updating its check byte, or the game discards the change on reload.
